column3: Classification for all real 3-manifolds, not just existence of one immersion. An h-principle would still require the formal totally-real bundle-map homotopy classification over F12; no small certificate or computed obstruction group here.

Universal connected closed PSC manifolds and every odd p. p-atoral needs its precise cohomological coefficient and orientability conventions; scalar-curvature obstruction in selected dimensions cannot establish all dimensions.

Ten points is finite but ambient dimension, stratum equivalence and degeneration conventions are missing. Listing sample tensegrities cannot classify every stratum; potentially large realizability classification, parked.

Every smooth Riemannian surface and a global isometric embedding into R4. Local embeddings or higher ambient dimensions do not meet global injectivity and regularity requirements; no bounded full-scope route.

All positive-characteristic fields and arbitrary-dimensional varieties. Perfectness and type of resolution need fixing; known low-dimensional mechanisms would be parameter instances, not a full-dimensional resolution.

Fragment asks exact Hermite constants in every remaining dimension. Determinant normalization and lattice quantifiers absent; a single packing or dimension gives only a bound or instance, not these exact constants.

For each cardinal lambda a common mu must work for every AEC of LS at most lambda and every larger categoricity cardinal. Amalgamation or tameness special cases change hypotheses; no short all-AEC route.

The concrete subquestion is direct beta=2 Tracy-Widom derivation from the stochastic Airy operator, amid a broad research program. Requires operator-domain and Brownian-potential definitions; merely importing ensemble equivalence is not a direct derivation. Successor bodies not checked.

Every sign vector length k; least prime, deterministic polynomial time in specified input encoding. CRT gives congruence classes, not an efficient least-prime certificate; p_i and cost encoding are not fixed literally.

For every fixed nonzero nonsquare integer n, finitely many D(n)-quadruples. Integral/positive/distinct conventions essential. Pell growth of one extension is not a global finiteness bound; cached landing page lacks needed question passage.

Existence of four distinct nonzero rationals, all ten unordered products including four diagonal squares. Ordinary Diophantine quadruples only check six off-diagonal products. Rational parametrization of each diagonal leaves simultaneous cross constraints; no full certificate. Cached landing page does not state this question.

The literal record omits inequality (2.11) and assumptions on psi. Primary HTML supplies continuous positive psi with q psi(q) nonincreasing, but renders (2.11) with greater-than sign, conflicting with approximation interpretation. Do not repair the inequality or promote a transcription refutation; primary fidelity HOLD.

One absolute positive c for every integer a>=2, nearest-integer norm of natural log. Primary Conjecture2.14 matches and explains product-log versus sum-log obstruction. Pointwise transcendence gives nonzero distances, not this uniform polynomial lower bound.

For every increasing positive exponent sequence and every prime witnessing algebraic irrational F_p series, conclude transcendence of its decimal sum. Read primary Conjecture5.4 and successor Theorem7. Indicator digits are 0/1, so no carries or p-reduction ambiguity; irrational series forbids eventual periodicity; Theorems2/7 apply with base10. Published full-scope subsumption, zero credit. Theorem2 local proof read; full Subspace-Theorem dependency not replayed.

Every finite field, but sufficiently many is not a numerical lower bound or density. Prime counts in Hasse intervals do not alone furnish prescribed curve counts; source and size threshold missing, HOLD.

A systematic taxonomy updating Joux2002 has no formal completeness or equivalence standard. One new assumption or diagram cannot resolve an unspecified taxonomy; source-dependent research program, HOLD.

Arbitrary-to-cyclic/ideal lattice reductions need problem, approximation factor, rank and polynomial-time model. Ideal structure is not supplied by changing a basis; selected embeddings do not settle all computational lattice problems.

All even integers k for a p-adic zeta function with unspecified branch/normalization and prime scope. Interpolation/trivial-zero conventions matter; no blanket nonvanishing deduction without the exact definition.
Every integer in residues5,6,7 modulo8 must be congruent. Passing to squarefree part is a routine invariance, not a construction of a rational right triangle for all squarefree inputs; no full route.
Every odd prime and k>=1 for s, plus k>=2 for d. s and d absent from literal definitions. Do not substitute familiar functions or claim prime-power experiments as all-prime proofs.
All k>=1 with named exceptional k=2. s,d,u_k undefined. A recurrence or small powers cannot be audited against these symbols without primary definitions; HOLD.

Every totally real field and prime, both lambda and mu vanish in the cyclotomic tower. Abelian or selected prime results do not cover arbitrary totally real fields; no uniform class-group stabilization mechanism.

Every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large T, not a subsequence; odd-order zeta zero within T^(1/4+epsilon). Averaged zero density and computed zeros cannot force every such interval; analytic barrier, parked.

Every integer, allowing signed integral cubes. Mod9 excludes some three-cube residues but four cubes escape that local obstruction. Finite search supplies no all-integer construction; positivity reinterpretations would change scope.
Every even integer>4208, both summands prime and each has a twin. Computation cannot provide uniform twin-prime representations; ordinary Goldbach or one twin prime summand is insufficient.

Converse of a named theorem without the particular congruence or domain restrictions. Wolstenholme has multiple equivalent prime forms whose composite converses differ; no safe literal counterexample scope without source.

Existence of any base47 Wieferich prime could have a tiny modular certificate. Needs precise odd-prime/base-coprime convention and existing published tables before any novelty claim. No search or certificate executed; named Wikipedia lead alone is not primary clearance.

For every prime eventual appearance in the Euclid-Mullin sequence; recursive least-prime choice is global. Divisibility of a primorial-plus-one at selected stages gives no eventual all-prime coverage bound.
All number fields and primes, mu vanishes. Tower and branch must be fixed explicitly; totally real/abelian restrictions or special prime calculations cannot prove this universal assertion.

For every odd p and every positive rank t, a p-rational multiquadratic field. Producing one quadratic field or an unbounded family at fixed p,t does not provide the uniform rank construction with p-rationality.

Every epsilon and every sufficiently large T, at least c H odd-order zeros for H=T^(1/2+epsilon). A single zero per interval or a long-interval density estimate is strictly weaker; no short analytic route.

Every d>2 and every open D containing0. Literal allows infinite exit time; then X_tau and directions are undefined. Sphere/hemisphere conclusion for finite exits still requires fine boundary analysis; excluded endpoint/domain correction earns no credit.

Two distinct assertions for planar Brownian trace: finite-intersection Jordan arcs for every complementary pair and total disconnectedness of buried points. A proof of one does not resolve both; universal random topology needs substantial continuum arguments.

All bounded connected open D, every particle system under intended N>=2. N=1 has no survivor and simultaneous deaths need conventions. Smooth-boundary nonexplosion does not establish irregular domains; no full coupling/Lyapunov control.

Condition on exactly two peaks and show rescaled graph distance tends to0 in law. Title's repel wording is opposite the literal concentration direction; do not silently replace it by macroscopic separation. Needs primary scope before combinatorial enumeration.

One online algorithm and universal constant for all monotone strictly-subadditive batch costs and all type waiting costs with finite optimum. Input distribution, information model and zero-optimum division need definitions; a fixed batching rule cannot be asserted universally competitive.

All starting offsets x classified for a common singular non-discrete non-spread-out step law. Eventual exact equality is stronger than approximate or distributional coupling; support-difference conditions alone do not establish successful finite-time coalescence.

Setwise convergence on the entire measurable path sigma-field of shifts, not finite-dimensional marginals, must imply TV. Oscillating density examples for arbitrary measures need realization as a single shift orbit; no valid shift-orbit construction established.

Conditional on failure of the preceding implication, seek a characterization for all measurable path sets. A Skorokhod weak-convergence representation does not characterize setwise convergence, and a counterexample alone is not this characterization.

All bounded-degree infinite connected graphs, one c for every S and ball. Empty S makes strict0>0 fail literally; trivial wording refutation excluded. Under intended positive intersections, ordinary Cheeger expansion is not uniform expansion inside every ball; parked substantive scope.

All locally finite bi-infinite configurations and force balance at every point. Need increasing indexing and absolute summation convention; permuting a lattice only exploits omitted ordering. Maximum-gap comparison needs an attained extremum or compactness; local finiteness alone gives neither uniform gaps nor global force control.

Literal pairwise additive distortion admits singleton graph with constant map. Missing coarse-surjectivity/unboundedness makes this a wording correction, not discovery. Under intended plane-model scope, rounded Euclidean distances need not arise as unweighted graph geodesics with uniform additive error.

Every Cayley graph admits some finite radius forcing a cover of every matching locally modeled graph. Local ball isomorphisms need coherent gluing; finite presentation or simple connectivity assumptions cannot be inserted. r363 concerns different Cayley-pattern family, not a mathematical subsumption of this record.

Combines two ball-rigidity thresholds and an independent random vertex-transitive degree concentration question. Size k versus radius versus diameter is not fixed and uniform labeled/unlabeled sampling differs. Solving one clause is not full-record resolution.

Every infinite vertex-transitive graph. Infinite path has pc=1 and critical percolation is connected, so literal scope needs pc<1/non-one-dimensional restriction; this domain correction earns no credit. Remaining critical-cluster assertion has no short full route here.

Every infinite vertex-transitive graph, equivalence of pc<pu and positive Cheeger constant. Need locally finite graph and Bernoulli model conventions; standard amenable direction alone is only half the question, no full nonamenable proof developed.

Two simple random walks in each of dimensions3 and4, starting at graph distance10, require an arbitrary coupling with positive probability of disjoint ranges. Transience of each walk does not give nonintersection of two independent ranges or a coupling; no mechanism for both dimensions.

Every bounded-triangle triangulation of either plane with matching ambient-isometric radius-r neighborhoods at vertices. Local star agreement does not provide global coherent isometries; periodicity has different Euclidean/hyperbolic group meanings, needs source definition.

Two mutually avoiding common-clock walks, planar trapping and all higher-dimensional nontrapping almost surely. Initial positions, tie/simultaneous step convention and trapped meaning need fixing; transience of ordinary walks does not govern this history-dependent process.

For every finite C one constant c<1 works for every finite simple graph and arbitrary start. Dubroff-Kahn2109.01237v1 Theorem1.1 gives precisely exp(-epsilon n), so c=exp(-epsilon) gives requested bound. Read theorem, Theorem1.2, Corollary1.4 proof and selected Section3 proof passages. This is published resolution; full partition proof/dependency replay not performed. Tiny n degeneracies are wording limits, no credit.
